description: Rules from spec/90-extensions/swhid.md: the opt-in bridge that cites a Software Heritage identifier (SWH-1..SWH-6). Every vector names the bridge it exercises (CON-28), so an implementation that does not claim it skips them. SWH-7 and SWH-8 are consumer obligations and are exempted in exemptions.json. The base claim is the true SWHID of fixtures/hello.txt, recomputed by tests/test_validate.py so that it cannot go stale.

vectors.name: swhid/claim-must-be-an-object
vectors.description: A bare identifier leaves no room for future bridge metadata and cannot be distinguished from a string another extension might define.

vectors.name: swhid/claim-must-not-be-null
vectors.description: JSON null is not an object and not an absent member: a record that writes the key with no claim is rejected, exactly as the schema types it.

vectors.name: swhid/swhid-is-required
vectors.description: A claim that names no identifier points at nothing; the SWHID is the only thing this bridge records.

vectors.name: swhid/core-identifier-must-have-forty-hex-digits
vectors.description: The fourth field of a core identifier is 40 hexadecimal digits (§4); a truncated hash names nothing.

vectors.name: swhid/scheme-version-must-be-one
vectors.description: The grammar defines scheme version 1 only (§4). A future version would need its own bridge revision, not a lenient parser.

vectors.name: swhid/object-type-must-be-known
vectors.description: The five object types are closed (§5.1); 'blob' is git's word for the object, not a SWHID type tag.

vectors.name: swhid/hex-digits-must-be-lowercase
vectors.description: SWHID's grammar admits only 'a'-'f' (§4) and the reference implementation emits lowercase, so grammar and ecosystem agree here, unlike the C2PA URN.

vectors.name: swhid/whitespace-is-not-part-of-the-grammar
vectors.description: An identifier is a token; a trailing space means the value was pasted from prose and is not the identifier the archive emitted.

vectors.name: swhid/qualifier-names-are-closed
vectors.description: The grammar defines six qualifier names (§6.2, §6.3); an unknown name is not a SWHID qualifier, and accepting it would let a record carry unchecked claims.

vectors.name: swhid/qualifier-must-have-a-value
vectors.description: A qualifier is a key/value pair; an empty value carries no information and §6.5 recommends omitting a redundant qualifier rather than emptying it.

vectors.name: swhid/visit-requires-origin
vectors.description: A visit names a snapshot of a specific origin; without the origin the reference has no meaning (§6.3.3).

vectors.name: swhid/visit-must-name-a-snapshot
vectors.description: The visit qualifier is the core identifier of a snapshot (§6.3.3); a revision there names the wrong kind of object.

vectors.name: swhid/path-is-only-valid-for-contents-and-directories
vectors.description: A path locates a content or a directory inside a tree; on a revision it is ignored by SWHID (§6.3.4), and a producer must not generate it (§6.1).

vectors.name: swhid/path-must-be-absolute
vectors.description: The grammar takes an ipath-absolute from RFC 3987 (§4); a relative path has no root to be read from.

vectors.name: swhid/anchor-requires-path
vectors.description: The anchor is the node a path is relative to; alone it designates nothing (§6.3.5).

vectors.name: swhid/anchor-must-not-be-a-content
vectors.description: An anchor is a directory, revision, release or snapshot (§6.3.5); a content has no root directory from which to read a path.

vectors.name: swhid/qualifiers-must-not-repeat
vectors.description: Each qualifier appears at most once (§6.2.1, §6.3.1); two origins would make the observation ambiguous.

vectors.name: swhid/origin-must-be-a-uri
vectors.description: An origin is a URI as RFC 3986 defines one (§6.3.2); a bare host name says where to guess, not where the object was observed.

vectors.name: swhid/fragment-lines-is-forbidden
vectors.description: A record identifies one artifact (ID-9); lines 9-15 are a fragment of it, not it, and the claim would leave the record's subject ambiguous.

vectors.name: swhid/fragment-bytes-is-forbidden
vectors.description: Same rule for the byte range: 'bytes' narrows a content the way 'lines' does (§6.2.3), and this bridge records whole artifacts only.

vectors.name: swhid/the-claim-defines-one-member
vectors.description: A resolver URL is derivable from the identifier; copying it into the claim creates a second statement that can disagree with the first.

vectors.name: swhid/id-must-not-be-a-swhid
vectors.description: Identity is the digest (ID-7, ID-8); a SWHID is stable across re-packaging, which is exactly why a reader cannot recompute it from the bytes.

vectors.name: swhid/digest-must-not-be-a-swhid
vectors.description: A cnt SWHID hashes a blob header plus the bytes (§5.2), so recording it as artifact.digest states a hash of a different pre-image.

vectors.name: swhid/minimal-content-claim-is-accepted
vectors.description: The base claim: the true SWHID of the fixture's bytes, with no qualifiers. One member, nothing copied.

vectors.name: swhid/directory-object-is-accepted
vectors.description: A source tree is a directory object; the hex is the tree identifier SWHID's own specification publishes as an example (§5.3).

vectors.name: swhid/release-object-is-accepted
vectors.description: A tag object is a release object (§5.5); this one is SWHID's published example of the Darktable 2.3.0 release.

vectors.name: swhid/snapshot-object-is-accepted
vectors.description: A snapshot object names a set of branch targets (§5.6); its type tag is accepted like any other.

vectors.name: swhid/full-context-is-accepted
vectors.description: A directory with all four context qualifiers, in SWHID's canonical order: origin, visit, anchor, path (§6.5).

vectors.name: swhid/percent-encoded-semicolon-is-accepted
vectors.description: Section 4 requires ';' inside a value to be escaped as %3B, so splitting on ';' is unambiguous and the escape must survive untouched.

vectors.name: swhid/path-case-is-not-normalised
vectors.description: Only the hexadecimal field is case-constrained; a path is a byte string and a validator that lowercased it would be over-strict.

vectors.name: swhid/a-shape-valid-swhid-need-not-match-the-digest
vectors.description: This record validator never sees the artifact's bytes, so it cannot relate a cnt SWHID to the digest. Checking that pair is SWH-7's consumer obligation, and rejecting here would be a false claim of verification.

vectors.name: swhid/a-record-without-the-claim-says-nothing
vectors.description: An unclaimed record for an artifact that happens to be archived is still a core record; the bridge is opt-in, and silence is not a denial.
